headline: Thanksgiving Takeaways
thesis: A quiet holiday news day puts the focus on governing AI already inside school tools, from vendor feature creep to Google's Nov. 30 Search deadline.
summary: Most sources published nothing new on Thanksgiving Day, so this edition rounds up the week. EdTech Magazine warns districts about AI feature creep: approved tools gaining AI functions after vetting. It recommends AI inventories, risk tiers and vendor notice before rollout. EdSurge looks at AI gaps in Title I schools and at continuity from early childhood into kindergarten. Google still faces a Nov. 30 deadline to answer Sen. Markey about tying school Search to its AI features. In higher ed, an NBER survey finds 23% of students admit using AI to draft essays but 54% say peers do, and new science and health graduate enrollment fell about 10%. Standards work continues with the QTI survey (Nov. 30), the CLR 2.0 showcase (Dec. 3) and Blackboard's Dec. 31 LTI 1.3 cutover.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 26, 2026 · Thanksgiving Day: no source published new items today, so this week's most recent items are shown. Direct page fetches were blocked in this run, so research used web search and dates come from search listings.

themes.title: AI, Writing & Academic Trust

themes.title: Trust, Evidence & EdTech Buying

themes.title: Higher Ed Enrollment & Governance
themes.body: New science and health grad enrollment fell about 10%, alongside leadership turnover and federal pressure on campuses.

themes.body: The QTI survey (Nov. 30), the CLR 2.0 showcase (Dec. 3), the LTI 1.3 cutover (Dec. 31) and Ed-Fi API v8.1 set the year-end agenda.
